actions.reason: Trims per-call and import overhead on the Base58Check path in base58/__init__.py without changing behaviour. (1) b58decode_check caches per-alphabet decode info in two dicts, one per autofix truthiness, instead of building and hashing a (alphabet, bool(autofix)) tuple key on every call. It uses direct fallback branches instead of a -1 sentinel, and checks the checksum without building a tuple. (2) b58encode_check returns the encoded result directly when there are no leading zero bytes (the common case), skipping a bytes multiply and concatenation. (3) Both decode fast paths pad the digit string to a multiple of 8 with a precomputed prefix tuple indexed by len & 7, replacing the negate/modulo/branch/multiply. (4) Drops `from __future__ import annotations`, which imports the __future__ module at runtime. The non-builtin annotations are now string literals, so nothing new is evaluated at def time. Outputs are identical. Measured check_ir ratio 0.9876; decode_ir 0.9955, encode_ir 0.9996.

journal.text:
I went after check_ir on the base58 lineage by trimming per-call overhead in b58decode_check and import overhead in base58/__init__.py. The decode-info cache moved from a tuple key of (alphabet, bool(autofix)) to two dicts, one per autofix truthiness. I replaced the -1 sentinel with direct fallback branches, compared the checksum without building a tuple, and dropped typing imports.

Evaluations 1, 3 and 5 were rejected for no improvement, with check_ir ratios of 0.9959, 0.9921 and 0.9900 against a required 0.9900. Evaluation 7, at 58 changed lines, was accepted in my sandbox: check_ir went from 999980203 to 987541240 (0.9876), and decode_ir came in at 0.9955. Outputs were identical every time. I submitted it, and it is queued for replay.

I think the checksum path is close to floor and the remaining cost is in the bignum decode itself. My gains are thin and sit near the threshold, so replay noise could erase them.

Next I should look at the core decode loop rather than call overhead.
